utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Mikulicic, are you ready to continue your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour. Good morning, Mr. Theunens. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, yesterday we left off while we were discussing disciplinary courts and disciplinary procedure. I want to show you another document now. I would kindly ask the registrar to show us 3D01-0634. 3D01-0634. Mr. Markac's Defence turned to the administration in charge of cooperation with international courts back in 2005 requesting clarification from the Ministry of the Interior on the issue of the functioning of disciplinary -- the disciplinary courts of the Ministry of the -- of Defence in the material period for the indictment. We received a document in which it is stated that under the then Law on the Interior there were disciplinary courts that were formed in first instance in each of the police administrations as well as the seat of the ministry, and there was a second instance court which was also housed at the seat of the ministry. From this explanation we conclude that it was prescribed that the disciplinary -- a disciplinary court has to have a president and additional two members in the police administration, a post was envisaged for a clerk in charge of disciplinary measures and proceedings, and the presidents and members of these courts were appointed through a decision of the Ministry of the Interior. Mr. Theunens, would you agree that this directs us to the regulation of the Law on the Interior from 1991 we saw yesterday which was D1077.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, were you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not seen the document that is on the screen, but I see a reference to Article 84 and Article 84 of the 1107 discusses the composition of -- it is translated there as disciplinary tribunals, but I understand it is the same as disciplinary courts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have not seen a two-page A4 document, then of course, first of all, you should read it in its entirety, that's one. And second, Mr. Mikulicic, documents explaining how it was, that's a kind of evidence where one could wonder whether this fits in the system. It is a statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It is an official statement of the Ministry of Interior, Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but does that change anything as far as the status of the document? I mean, tomorrow we get a document in which matters are explained to us what happened in Knin or -- official or not. The evidentiary status of such a statement, which comes close to a 92 bis statement, 92 ter statement, it was prepared for the purpose of these proceedings, from what I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No. We ask for the information of the -- through the -- through the Office for the Cooperation of International Courts of the Minister of Interior, how was the legislation upon the constitution of disciplinary courts within the Ministry of Interior, and we got this answer, which is in line with the provisions of the law 1077 made yesterday in this courtroom. So I offer this document as in evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. Given the provenance and explanation by Mr. Markac [sic], I do not object to its admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you wanted to refer to Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. I'm sure I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, the Chamber first wants to read the document in its entirety and -- but it can be marked for identification. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1079, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's the status the document will keep for the time being. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could I have document 3D01-0721.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, were you able to see this document before or a similar document? This is a decision on appointing president and deputy president as well as members of the disciplinary court at first instance of the police administration Zadar-Knin. Have you had occasion to see this decision or a similar one?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen this decision or a similar one before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This is a decision by the Minister of the Interior, Mr. Ivan Jarnjak, pursuant to Article 84 that we have just seen of the Law on the Interior appointing a -- members to a first instance court at the police administration of Zadar and Knin. We see that president, deputy president, and members were appointed.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I tender this document into the evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I have no objection to this document in relation to the previous one. It might be helpful if we could see the request by the Markac Defence, which was dated 9th of December, because that may set out the exact terms under which the letter was supposed to be sent. It's almost like an RFA, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: That's no problem with us, Your Honour. I will provide the request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll further hear from you, Mr. Waespi, once you've seen it. Madam Registrar, the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit D1080.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1080 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: May I have document, Madam Registrar, 3D01-0719.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, we said already that disciplinary courts were set up at police administrations in first instance as well as at the seat of the ministry at first instance. This decision is the same as the previous one, the only difference being that this concerns the appointment of president and deputy president of the first instance court at the seat of the ministry. Have you had occasion to see this type of decisions previously?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I didn't have the occasion to see such decisions before. I note this one dates from August 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The decision is from 1997, but you can see in the preamble that it is pursuant to Article 84 of the Law on the Interior, that is to say the same law that was the basis for the previous decision from 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I tender this document into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, Exhibit D1081.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1081 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Madam Registrar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, the question -- the observation made by the witness a second ago that this was a document from 1997 I think stems from the witness not knowing exactly what your case is in this respect, apparently that there was a system of disciplinary courts in the Ministry of the Interior. Now, of course the question is legislation was there. People were appointed in those courts, which does not come as a surprise but it is good to establish that. Is it your case that these courts dealt with certain matters where in the indictment we find that Mr. Markac or others are held responsible for not doing anything? What's exactly your case in this respect? If the witness would know, then -- and I think he's entitled to know, then it will be -- it will certainly smoothen the communication during your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honour. I will come to it. Madam Registrar, may I have the document 3D01-0717.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the last document on the topic of the setting up of disciplinary courts and appointing of presidents and members. Here we have a decision on appointing the president of the second instance disciplinary court at the seat of the ministry, that is to say the court that dealt with appeals pursuant to the Law on the Internal Affairs following decisions rendered by first instance court -- courts. I suppose, Mr. Theunens, that you did not have an opportunity to see this type of decisions issued by the minister, Mr. Jarnjak, either.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay. May I have -- tender this document into the evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1082, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1082 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: As we saw, Mr. Theunens, within the ministry there were first and second instance disciplinary courts. Who was it within the Ministry of the Interior, including the special police as part of the ministry, of course, who was responsible for the implementation of disciplinary regulation in the police units themselves? I want to put up a document indicating that, and then I will kindly ask for your comment. The document is P587. It is a Prosecution document. Therefore, I suppose you did see it before. Let us wait for it for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Mikulicic please speak into the microphone to his right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, you're invited --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will do my best, Your Honour. It is P587. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, this is an order issued by assistant minister Mr. Mladen Markac in November 1995. It was sent to the chiefs of all police administrations except for the Virovitica, Podravina and Medjimurje police administration. It was to be served on the commanders of SJP units as well as to the head of the special police sector, to the commander of the anti-terrorist unit Lucko and the airborne unit commander. Mr. Theunens, do you have an explanation as to why this document specifically states that it was not to be delivered to the Virovitica, Podravina and Medjimurje police administrations? Why were they exempt from the delivery list? Do you have an explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no explanation for that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Would you accept an explanation that I want to offer, and that is that in those police administrations there were no special police units.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would indeed be a logical explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This document mentions a ministerial collegium whereby the issue of working discipline was discussed within the organisational units of the MUP and that certain type of behaviour was in existence, and in keeping with that, Mr. Markac, assistant minister, issued this order placing the responsibility on the heads of departments and commanders in items 1, 2, 3, and 4 to supervise their employees and that they are responsible for the implementation of this order. Is it a conclusion of your expertise that based on this document the commanders of units and heads of administrations were those people who were tasked with supervising the discipline in the units that they commanded?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I would just like to add that the duty of the special police unit commander as well as the anti-terrorist unit commander to enforce discipline and maintain discipline in his unit is also specified in the November 1995 rules on internal organisation of the Ministry of Interior which correspond with 65 ter 5032. It may have been tendered, but in any event, it is discussed in the addendum, pages 7 and 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation, Mr. Theunens. We will get to that document as well. When you were studying the documents for this case and based on your previous knowledge and experience, do you know what substantive law was applied by the disciplinary courts within the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not specifically analysed this aspect, i.e., the types or the kinds of substantive law applied by the disciplinary courts within the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know what procedural law was applied by these disciplinary courts?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have -- again, I have not analysed these legal aspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, yesterday we saw the Law on Courts stipulating all of the courts in the Republic of Croatia. Do you agree with me that in that law there is no mention of any disciplinary courts, that is to say that disciplinary courts were not made part of the regular judiciary system in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, Your Honours. I have no clear recollection of the law we discussed yesterday. I saw it on the screen here, but I haven't looked further into it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Mikulicic kindly turn off the microphone to his right or speak directly into the microphone to his left. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In the Law on Courts what was envisaged was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you receive the message which asked you to switch off one of your microphones to the right and to speak in the one to your left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Well, I have microphone on my left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And I will try to put it closer to me. I think that will be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic has to speak into the microphone, Your Honour. We can't hear him very clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, I do understand that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... some trouble with my microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I see for one reason or another there is a problem with your microphone because the interpreters cannot hear you, and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Is this one okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, every microphone is okay as long as one speaks into it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Mikulicic, the answer is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Every microphone --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you turn your head in another direction than where the microphone is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay. I hope that will be fine. Is it now okay for the booth?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Much better. Thank you very much, Your Honour and Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Much better. Okay. I'm sorry for that technical problem that I made.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, let me put the question this way: We agree, therefore, that disciplinary courts were not part of the regular judiciary of the Republic of Croatia and that they were set up in keeping with the Law on the Interior within the ministry itself. In and of itself the ministry is a civilian body, is it not, the Ministry of the Interior I mean.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there are two questions included in --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] In one.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in one. The first part it's possible. I mean if you say so, I have no reason to doubt its veracity. For the second part, yes, the Ministry of Interior is a civilian body.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Disciplinary courts were therefore envisaged as administrative courts, and in Croatia there was judicial overview of the disciplinary proceedings conducted by disciplinary courts within the ministry. Are you familiar with that topic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am not familiar with that topic. I -- as you can see from my report, I focused on the role of -- in the context of special police of the unit commanders as well as the chief of sector and the assistant Minister of Interior in the enforcement of discipline among their subordinates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In keeping with the Law on Courts we saw yesterday, in Croatia there was an administrative court of the Republic of Croatia then as it is now. Do you know what its competences are?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not familiar with the competencies of the administrative court of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If I told you that the jurisdiction of the administrative court of the Republic of Croatia, which is a part of the judiciary in keeping with the Law on Courts, then its role is to control the decisions made by the disciplinary courts within the ministry. Judicial review on part of the administrative law of the Republic of Croatia could be asked for if there was reason to appeal the decision of the second instance court within the ministry. Were you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, it is true, is it not, if we were to accept your definition as expert witness and the jurisprudence of this Tribunal, that as regards the military judiciary disciplinary courts and measures you do not have any expert knowledge?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that, Your Honours. I have not discussed or analysed the organisation -- excuse me. The question says military judiciary disciplinary courts. Is that the question or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] It is. Military and police disciplinary courts.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned earlier, I have included what I believe to be the main regulations that apply to the military disciplinary courts as well as military disciplinary prosecution and after that also the military courts and military prosecutors. I have not analysed these bodies as such, and I did not include information in my report on the disciplinary courts within the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is clear, Mr. Theunens, but my question, however, was whether you personally believe that you have the necessary expert knowledge to cover the topic of disciplinary courts and the organisation of the military judiciary that we discussed yesterday and today.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't believe it's up to me to answer that question. I have explained already on the first day of my testimony what my background is, I mean background on the educational and training level, as well as my professional experience, and -- yeah, that concludes my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes. [Interpretation] Just to remind you, Mr. Theunens, on the 19th of November this year, during examination-in-chief which is transcript page 12155, line 17, when answering to a question put by Mr. Waespi you said that -- after being asked by Mr. Waespi whether you have any knowledge on the civilian aspect and whether you believe yourself to be an expert for civilian structures, you said: [In English] "It's a difficult question because obviously from my work at ICTY I did not have that expertise." [Interpretation] To jog your memory even further, Mr. Theunens, on the 1st of December this year, transcript page 12871, line 19, you said: [In English] "I am not a legal expert." [Interpretation] Keeping these statements of yours in mind, my question is this: As regards the topics we have discussed, do you hold yourself out to be an expert or not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would just like to come back to what Mr. Mikulicic commented earlier. It is correct that I gave the answer to Mr. Waespi in relation to the civilian authorities, but civilian authorities includes a lot. It includes local administration. It includes political authorities. It includes --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, it includes also judicial matters and so on and so on. I consider myself qualified to review documents that apply to military discipline and military justice. Why? Because I have a military background. I'm a professional officer, and I have, as I mentioned yesterday, seated in court-martial. Now, I agree with you that I have not reviewed the civilian disciplinary courts, i.e., disciplinary courts in the Ministry of Interior, and I certainly do not consider myself an expert on disciplinary courts be it military or civilian, because I would assume that to be an expert in legal matters you would need to have a legal degree, at least at the master's level and probably higher, but that's just my personal view.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your answer. We'll turn to a different topic now, Mr. Theunens, namely the organisation and structure of the Ministry of Interior, with the emphasis on the organisation and structure of the special police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is a document that frequently appeared on our screens and this is a diagram of the Ministry of the Interior with the emphasis on the Zadar-Knin police administration. You have had occasion to see it in the courtroom and earlier on I suppose, is that true?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it the first time I believe it was yesterday that you showed it or at least this week I saw it for the first time. I don't know what it is based or maybe there are any footnotes or something or whether it's taken from an existing regulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is a document of the Prosecution, and it was my assumption, since you reviewed OTP documents for the purposes of this case, that you saw this document too. Nevertheless, let us take a look.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I please -- the documents I -- I reviewed are documents that were held by the Prosecution; but when you use the name Prosecution documents, to me that means documents produced by the Prosecution, i.e., compiled or drafted by members of the Prosecution and that is something I did not -- I did not see this chart before you -- I believe it was you showed it to me yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you for reminding me, Your Honour. Then it will be under seal, this document, so I will ask for the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, not to be shown to the public, and if -- there's so many names on it that I have difficulties in reconstructing exactly why, but perhaps if you put specific questions in relation to persons because it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't put specific questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is just the structure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The structure, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the structure as such is not protected. However, names are. So if there's ever any moment that you want to refer to names would you please ask us first to go into private session. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, what I'm interested in at the moment is the position within the schematics of the special police unit of the Zadar-Knin police administration. Can we conclude -- will you agree with me that in -- according to this diagram the special police unit was attached to the police administration headed by the chief of the police administration?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, Your Honours. First of all, I do not know who put the chart together and what the lines mean. At some locations there are dotted or interrupted lines. Other locations there are straight lines. The special police unit is, for one reason or the other, put on the left side, whereas other police units or regular police units are put underneath the Zadar-Knin police administration. Therefore, that is for what the chart is concerned. Now, for what my report is concerned, on English page 106, part 1 of the report, I put that the special police units that are located in the police administrations are "directly subordinated to the chief of special police sector." And one of the sources I use for that is P588.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic. Mr. Mikulicic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, can we go into private session for a minute, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in answer to my question you referred to a section of your report, and you mentioned page 106, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. Part 1 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a title "See subordination of the special police."

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then "Including reported -- reporting," excuse me. And then under the title 2, between brackets, I have put "The special police units in the police administrations," and I put, between brackets, behind it "counties" or "zupanijas." Then, "Directly subordinated to the chief of special police sector."

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Theunens. What is concerning me that this is page 107 in my version of your report, but nevertheless, it's the very same portion. You referred to the 65 ter 1417; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, yeah. I've -- it -- it is document P588.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is this brochure of the Ministry of Interior which was at the time the only document I had available to determine the -- the de jure situation, and of course in part 2 of the report, in the section on special police, which section 4, I address the operations conducted by special police units and there I also discuss command and control and I come to the same conclusions, i.e., that special police units are subordinated to the Assistant Minister of Interior through the chief of special police sector and that the chiefs of local -- I mean the county police administrations play no role in that chain of command, control, and reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, I disagree with you. I disagree with your conclusion. My thesis and assertion is that the commanders of the special police units within the police administration were subordinated to the chief of that particular police administration. Can we see a part of the document, P588, which is a leaflet of the ministry of the interior which you refer to in one of your conclusions. Can you refer us to the part of the document that led you to make such a conclusion? P588.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We have the page with the ERN 0354-9987, which should correspond with page 29 of the document. And if I -- if I'm allowed, afterwards I can also clarify what I found in other documents, documents that became available to me later --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could we have page 29 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. I think there are page numbers at the bottom of the pages. And in the top right corner you probably -- you should see the ERN, and it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: ERN is 0354-9987; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So could we see this page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And then we scroll to the bottom, and we see the text under the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The special police, according to the inner structure, consists of the special police Sector with its departments, divisions, training centre, aviation unit, anti-terrorist unit Lucko, and other units which are located in police administrations, in accordance with the territorial organisation of the Republic of Croatia." This means that the special police units which are located in the police administrations are -- for hundred per cent part of the special police sector, and what is put in P588 is coherent with what we can find in 65 ter 5031, as well as Article 27 of 65 ter 6104, the last document being the February 1995 rule on the internal organisation and operations of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, with all due respect, I cannot accept at all your conclusion about the subordination of the special police units within police administrations. According to the chief of the special police sector -- well, in terms of discipline this is something that I can accept, and in terms of these being specialised -- very specialised units which have a unique structure and which, in their professional work, do represent a certain organic part of the Ministry of Interior. However, administratively speaking the special police units attached to police administrations are responsible to the chiefs of these police administrations both in terms of discipline and in any other sense including financing, assignment of missions and so on and so forth. This is something, however, that we will get back to during our cross, and I will show you some documents that we can comment upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this time I should like document 65 ter document 5032 to be called up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know whether the previous, yeah, question by Mr. Mikulicic required me to answer or I just ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] No. Mr. Theunens, I just show you my case --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: -- and my submissions on the topic.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I just would like to mention that the assignment of missions, when we are talking about the kind of missions that special police units conducted during Operation Storm and after Operation Storm, independent of the specific documents I have included in part 3 of the report -- excuse me, in part 2 of the report which show that the missions are assigned by General Markac or the chief of special police sector, these are certainly not administrative matters but these are operational matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, we will, of course, be coming back to that topic. Now that I've broached it, however, this is my question for you: Do you discern a difference in the functioning of the police -- special police structure in times of peace and in times of combat, or do you consider the structure to always be the same?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not found any specific regulation that determines or that allows to answer that question. I do know that prior to the start of Operation Storm, a special command structure, i.e., I think it was called a joint -- one second. I can find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Joint forces.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, a staff of joint forces of special police was established on the 22nd of July 19 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We will come to that Mr. Theunens. [Interpretation] My question was do you discern a difference or do you distinguish the peacetime structure of the police, special police, and the combat time structure? Do you see a difference there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the exception of the staff of the joint forces of special police, which is P554, I have not seen a document indicating that there is a distinction in the structure. But of course if you have a document, I would appreciate if you could show it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, I will show you, Mr. Theunens. Just let me find this document which is on the screen in my tab. [Interpretation] Have you ever seen the rules on the internal organisation of the Ministry of the Interior, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ones that are on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, indeed. I have included them on -- in the addendum to my report. I have a recollection, though, that the copy the OTP received, if this is 65 ter 5032, was incomplete, and I -- I remember requesting the team to provide -- I mean, the Prosecution team to provide a more complete copy because it is my impression that this document is a compilation of different documents, and that's why I have referred now, a few minutes ago, to 65 ter 6104, which is not addressed in my report nor in the addendum.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, I consider this document a very important one. However, in view of the translation of the document, it might be misleading. This is only to caution the Trial Chamber. Reviewing the document and observing some inept translations of parts of it, I contacted Mr. Waespi and drew his attention to the ineptly translated sections. It was concluded that the translation would be sent for revision to the translation service. However, you are here today, and we have the document before us. I will be using it with certain reservations that I will make. This document, among other things, describes the posts within the special police force, including the post of the commander of the special police unit, in other words, the unit which is within the police administration. The post has the designation M280, and we can find it at page 78 of the document, ERN number 06119723. Mr. Theunens, once we get the page on our screens I will draw your attention to the parts I consider ineptly translated.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can just -- I can just mention this is included on page 8 of the addendum, English page 8, and it's my understanding that it's the -- maybe it was a transcript issue. It was the command of a special police unit, i.e., the units that are located or co-located with the county police administrations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Right. [Interpretation] That's correct, Mr. Theunens, but we're still waiting for the relevant page to appear on our screens. You have it there with you or not? Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe there was some misunderstanding while I'm referring to the page 78, but it was page 78 marked on the same document as -- but the real ERN number should be brought up on the screen and this is, I repeat, 06119723. [Interpretation] Your Honours, let me acquaint you with the problem I've -- I've come across. This is a document describing the posts within the special police force. The document was translated in the view of the Defence in a -- in an inadequate matter, and I've raised as much in the two letters I sent to Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 280 appears on page 9 out of 24 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I drew the attention to the ineptly translated parts. First of all, the Croatian word "rukovodi" was translated in this document and in some other documents we will come to later in four different ways, of which the most frequent English word "command" was used. In some other documents, the word is translated as "rules", "runs," "directs," but nowhere in the entire document is there a Croatian word "zapovijedati" to be found. This is, however, something we will probably be dealing with outside the courtroom. I just wanted Their Honours to be aware of the translation issue which exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I suppose, Mr. Theunens, that you read the English translation of the document, and the English translation indicated the issue of "zapovijed" and "kontrola," the control -- the command and control, although nowhere in the Croatian original are the two terms used. The terms used are "rukovoditi" "organizirati," which can be translated as "directs," "organise," but nowhere in the document is the command and control expression used. Let us go back to the post of the commander of the special police unit where it is said that he directly -- he directs, not commands as it was translated, and is responsible for the work of the special police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, could you please repeat the word which does not appear clearly in the transcript, the word that was never used in this document as you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The word is "zapovijeda."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: That's command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's not the same as "zapovjednik."

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Zapovjednik" is the noun, and "zapovjedati" is the verb. In this case "zapovjednik," commander, is the title of the post. When the activity of the commander of the special police is described, nowhere does the text use the term "zapovjedati," "command." The terms used are "rukovoditi," "voditi [phoen]" -- manage a department, organise. Nowhere is the word "zapovjedati" used.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Also the title of M280 actually starts with "zapovjednik."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, what do you think triggered my question? Exactly that. It's not only for 280 but some of the following. But therefore, you'd say, Mr. -- first of all, we need a translation which is beyond dispute, that's one. And second, do I understand you, Mr. Mikulicic, that your position is that the use of a word which is quite close to the word you used is just the title and you focus on the description where that word does not appear? Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And what I would like is a precise translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Full support by the Chamber to get that precise translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: But above this there is another topic which is, from my point of view, even more important.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, in the description of the duties carried out by the commander of the special police unit of the police administration, a part of the text was omitted in the English translation which in my view is very significant. In the Croatian text that the relevant portion starts with the part where it is said that the commander is responsible for discipline. [In English] I don't know whether you can find it in the English text. It is a -- yes. It is a -- on the screen if you come from bottom to the top it's one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eighth line, where it starts "Responsible for discipline." Can you find it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it, because I have it also in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just trying to look in the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes. In -- [Interpretation] In the Croatian version it is followed by this text: That he's responsible for discipline and to establish positive interrelationships within the unit, and now comes the part of the text that was omitted in the English version. In Croatian it reads: "To propose to the chief of the police administration measures to suppress negative behaviour within the unit." That part was omitted. Would you agree with me, Mr. Theunens, that the description of the job post of the special police commander as described here puts that person in a position in which the police administration head is the figure of authority that he needs to turn to rather than to turn to the head of the special police sector at the ministry, pointing at the fact that there was no direct line of communication with the sector of special police in the ministry but, rather, that there was a relationship of subordination towards the head of the police administration within which the special police unit is functioning?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you that this sentence should have been included, obviously, in the English translation. Now, I'm -- it's difficult for me to establish what the role of the county police administration chief would be in that context, because as I have addressed on English page 107, part 1 of the report, there is within the special police administration -- excuse me, the special police sector, I apologise, a special department, namely the department for internal control that is, among other things, tasked with the verification of work discipline and internal order in the special police units, and the references can be found in D529, D528, which means that there is an exchange of information between the special police units and the internal control department, that the internal control department can, for example, also conduct inspections and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] I'm sorry to interrupt you, Mr. Theunens. We will come to the internal department in a few minutes, so let's focus on that topic for a moment?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I'm trying to answer the question. I mean, at first glance I'm surprised by the reference to the chief of the local, i.e., county police administration in connection to the maintaining or enforcement of discipline in special police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Within this police administration.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And its --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This is my comment. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, it's not only your comment but it doesn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: But you are overlapping as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we would not even know about your comment. If you say let's leave it like that, fine. If you'd like to have it on the record, please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Theunens, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I would want to see, then, more documents in order to see whether, for example, we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'll show you one.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have examples of a chief of special police unit communicating with the chief of the county police administration on matters that are -- appear to be covered by this sentence in the job description.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we mark this document for identification while we are waiting for the translation issue to be solved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Final translation. Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, that's no problem. We submitted it to the CLSS I think more than a week ago, and we consistently remind them, but they are overloaded with high priority tasks, so we just have to be patient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1083, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1083 keeps that status for the time being. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could we have on the screen 3D01-0713.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, what you are about to see on the screen is a document issued by the Ministry of the Interior, Mr. Ivan Vekic, by virtue of which the system of the special police in the Republic of Croatia was set up. First of all, did you ever see this document before?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I please see the top of the English page again, just for the date and the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] It's in your final addendum spreadsheet. The number is 20080918.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must have seen it. I was just checking where I have included it in my report, but anyway, to save time we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So, could we proceed? Okay. [Interpretation] This document was issued by the then Minister of the Interior, Mr. Ivan Vekic. It is an order. Under item 1 it states that due to special security reasons special police units are to be formed in each police administration. In item 2 it states that the special units are to be formed using the personnel and materiel and technical equipment of the former special police units. Which are those former special or separate police units? What is the minister referring to in item 2?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with the existence of a Lucko anti-terrorist unit which, according to P605 mentioned on English page 105 of part 1 of the report, was established in September 1990. And I have also a reference to special police units, or special police in general, dating from May 1991, and that comes from 65 ter 1182, which is the 27th of May, 1991, amendment to the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you for your answer, Mr. Theunens, but this is not answer to my question. We will come to the anti-terrorist unit Lucko afterwards. Now, my question is: Can you explain, in count 2 of this order, what is the reference to the portion of the text?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question, Your Honour -- Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will repeat it then. [Interpretation] By virtue of this order of the Minister of the Interior, special police units were set up at the level of each of the police administrations. That is clear, is it not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the order states.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Item 2: The special units are to be formed using the personnel and materiel and technical equipment of the former special police units. To remind you, Mr. Theunens, the State of Croatia was in its inception at the time, and it was supposed to establish all of its power structures including the special police. Prior to the existence of the Republic of Croatia, there existed certain special police units which had existed in the former Yugoslavia. Would you agree with me that at this point in time, through this decision by the minister, a continuation of the functioning of those former special police units was to be ensured and these were now the newly -- supposed to be the newly formed special police units? Would you accept that explanation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, so that they would be based on at least part of the former special police units, because I assume they were also special police units existing in parts that by the time of this specific order were under Serb control, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the anti-terrorist unit Lucko. However, it was specific in nature and position. It was within the sector of special police with the Ministry of the Interior, and it had no relation to any particular police administration. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed it is -- it is directly located at the level of the special police sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, in items 3 and 4 of the order, it is specified how many employees were required for the special police units. In item 5, a mention is made of a reserve special unit that was supposed to be formed equal in number to the active unit. In item 6, mention is made of the reserve special units which had to be formed from members of the reserve police forces in accordance with the criteria established for active-duty members of special units. Therefore, this refers to policemen, be it active-duty or reserve policemen; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Now we get to item 7 which reads: "Special units are to be engaged solely pursuant to decisions issued by the chief of a police administration and Deputy Minister of the Interior or the person thus authorised by him." I'd like to focus on the words "to be engaged solely pursuant to the decision issued by the chief of a police administration." Do you conclude, Mr. Theunens, based on that that the chief of a police administration is the person approving the use of the special police unit within the police administration headed by that person?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that this is indeed correct at the time of -- of this order, and I believe it was from November 1991. I can't see the date anymore. Yes. Yes. At the time of this order, it is like it is described in this paragraph 8 -- or, excuse me, 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If we go to item 8, which is the last item in the English, in the Croatian version it is page 2, it reads as follows: "The chief of a police administration, before engaging a special unit in the area of his administration, must obtain clearance from deputy minister or the person authorised by the deputy minister." Item 9 reads: "The special unit cannot be used in the area of another police administration without a decision made by the deputy minister or a person authorised by him."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we please scroll down in the English version a bit, or maybe the next page? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, it is the next page in English. It is count 9 I'm referring to. [Interpretation] Item 9 states as follows: If a special unit of a particular police administration is to be used outside the territory of that administration, the deputy minister must issue a decision approving that. Would you agree with that? That is what the order states?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, and I just want to reiterate that the order dates from the 15th of November, 1991, and the documents I have -- the other documents I have reviewed indicate that there have been changes over time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What are the changes you came across that would invalidate effectively this order? Which are those changes? In the documentation you reviewed did you come across at least a single document which would state that the head of a police administration has no authority to use a special police unit within the territory of his own police administration? Did you ever come across such a document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not come across such a document explicitly stating that. However, I would like to mention that this order from the 15th of November makes no reference to a special police sector whereby I would expect if a special police sector already existed at that time that a reference to that sector would be made. Secondly, without going into details, the documents I have reviewed that cover the operations of special police units prior, during, and after Operation Storm --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Mr. Theunens, this is completely different topic. This is the topic of the united forces of the special police while employing into the combat activities. We will come to it later on, but I believe in the meantime we will have a break now, in a minute, if you could, during the pause, try to find out document which stated that this particular document that I showed you has been diminished, cancelled or otherwise put out of the -- out of the order or out of the rule. Could I have number for this document, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections. I would just like to -- to request that the witness is allowed to finish at least the thought, the sentence he was about to explain what he has been asked, what changes were made, and not specifically reference to documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may react. The witness is obviously trying to avoid my direct questions and go to something completely different topic, and that's why I intervened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, first of all, you wanted this document to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- admitted into evidence. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1084, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Exhibit D1084 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Mikulicic, if a witness says that what he reads in a document in -- dating from 1991 might not be valid at a later stage, then to say, "Could you point at the document which specifically says that this 1991 document is not valid any more," et cetera, the witness is in a position where he can explain the changes he says were made or the changing situation, and although documentary evidence is very important in relation to that, I think you went a bit too far in limiting him in explaining what caused him to -- to take the view that the matter was not as it was in 1991 and specifically as described in that document. Mr. Theunens, if you'd like to further explain you have an opportunity to do so, and then we'll have a break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I just wanted to explain that the documents covering the operations of special police units prior to, during, and after Operation Storm, and I mean by that the documents I had the opportunity to review, did not make reference to the chiefs of the county or other local police administrations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I do understand that Mr. Mikulicic will take you to these documents at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, I agree with that completely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And will put further questions in relation to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Just one question if you allow me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Mikulicic, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, I completely agree with you. However, please focus on item 9 of the order which says if a special unit of the police is to be used in the area of another police administration then a decision on the part of the minister or the person authorised by him is needed. utterances.text: Yes. Now may I proceed?

utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to pull up on the screen the document P588, please, Madam Registrar -- or Mr. Registrar. Sorry. It is page 37 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, this is the portion of the document you refer to in your expertise. This is P588, and as we can see, it is a chart of the Zagreb police administration. Are you familiar with the chart?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, I'm familiar with the chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: At the time -- or, rather, at this moment I'm only interested in the top part of it. We can see that the head of the police administration is the person under whose competence the entire organisation of the police administration lies. Below him there is his deputy, his Chef de Cabinet. Then we have the analysis department, the department for analysis and criminal records, and the special police unit. Do you agree with me that it follows from the chart that the unit of the special police force is within the police administration subordinated to the head or chief of the police administration?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the chart has to be considered in -- in the context of what is mentioned on page - I'm looking for the exact reference - 9987 in this same brochure where it is stated, as I read out earlier, that indeed the special police units are located in the county police administrations, but they are subordinated or they are part of the special police sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Once again, Mr. Theunens, I do not accept your conclusion. Can document 3D01-0674 be called up, please. utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document indeed states that the assistant chief of the police administration in Zagreb proposes someone for a position in the special police unit. It is stated that he is a member of the police administration Zagreb currently working as a police official, specialist training instructor of the special police unit. Maybe it's a translation issue but it's not entirely clear to me whether he's effectively a member of the special --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the same happens again. You are going into details on matters which are not the core of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you, Mr. Mikulicic, or you, Mr. Theunens, refresh my recollection as to Article 62 of the Law on Interior Affairs, which --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- apparently is the basis for this proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It's a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have the exhibit number then --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It's a D1077.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'll find it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And the Article 62 stated that -- you will find yourself, Your Honour, but it is a duty of the Minister of Interior to rule upon the position of members of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So there's nothing in that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that assistance. Please proceed.

utterances.text: Could we mark this document as evidence, please.

utterances.text: D1085 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have 3D01-0676.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, this is a decision which on the basis of the proposal we earlier looked at was issued by Minister Jarnjak. Did you have the opportunity to see this document or a similar one?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I've seen this document or a similar document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Let us quickly go through the document. utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I wouldn't necessarily draw the conclusion Mr. Mikulicic is proposing, because there must be a communication also from the minister to the special police sector, because special police sector has to be informed one way or the other of the appointment of a commander of a special police unit based on the other material I have reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I agree with you. However, what we were able to see from the two documents is communication between the Minister of the Interior and the assistant chief of the police administration in relation to the appointment of a commander of the special police unit of that particular police administration. [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... into the evidence, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI

utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the category of separate police units, but maybe it's a translation issue.

utterances.text: Could I please have D465.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, did you come across this document while preparing your expertise?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]

Do you know what the purpose was of putting together separate police units of general duty police?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. That is an aspect I have not analysed. I have only reviewed the operations and related aspects that pertain to the special police, SJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could we go into private session for a moment, Your Honour?

utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay. I will repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does this explanation refresh your memory about the function and use of separate police units of the general duty police?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned, I have not analysed the -- or reviewed the activities of the regular police, including the separate police units. My focus was on the activities of the special police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could we have 65 ter 5619.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, allow me to direct your attention to one portion of the expertise. utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.text: We will now be discussing a different topic which you said you reviewed, which is the topic of the joint forces of the special police. It is true that you studied the topic, did you not, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: During the first session we saw a document which was given the number 1084, which was the order by Minister Vekic from 1991, which in actual fact constitutes an introduction to the establishment of the joint forces. utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is addressed in part 1 of the report, section 5, more specifically starting at English page 105. The terminology "joint" or the term "joint" is based on my review of the documents used, for example, prior, during, and after Operation Storm when we talk, for example, as is defined in P554, about the staff of the joint forces of the special police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that. Are you familiar with the way in way these joint forces were set up?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with the establishment of these joint forces prior to and during and after Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the -- that the joint forces were set up in such a way that the special police units from police administrations would set aside elements of their forces -- or, rather, a number of their members and in this way a joint team would be set up called joint forces? utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such -- such examples can indeed be seen during and after Operation Storm. And even prior to it, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could we have 3D01-0630.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document we're about to see dates from 1991. It was issued by Assistant Minister Mr. Josko Moric. It was addressed to the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia and the General Staff of -- or the Main Staff of the Croatian army. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe I've seen it. It doesn't -- it doesn't ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The document comes as a result of the reporting to the Ministry of Defence or the General Staff about how many policemen were engaged out of the police administrations in the combat activities at that period of time. It goes on to say that all these members of police administrations were placed under the command of the Croatian army. The relations between the Croatian army commanders and the police commanders had to be one of coordination and cooperation. However, when the police, upon a request of the commander of the Croatian army, is engaged in defence combat activities, the police units were to be placed under the command of the Croatian army, and all the requests for the use of police in combat, that's the last paragraph, should go through the General Staff and the Ministry of the Interior, which shall judge the expedience and approve their engagement in combat and carry out responsibility for it. This shows us in what way the police was used in combat. In this particular instance it includes both the general duty police and the special police. Mr. Theunens, in your role as an expert did you ever come across an example where the civilian forces of the police were used in war activities and placed under the command of the General Staff of the army which is in charge of combat activities? Did you ever come across such an example?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to clarify, when you ask civilian force of the police, that includes special police?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. I mean, the order prior to Operation Storm --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you. My question was whether you had find such example in some other areas apart from the Croatian situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This is speaking comparatively.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the SFRY All People's Defence Law foresaw that if police was to be used in combat operations they would be subordinated to the JNA, but otherwise I'm not familiar with particular proven examples, except for Croatia, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: May this document be tendered into the evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit number D1088. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1088 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: May I have 3D01-0656.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, let me explain the methodology I'm using. Through the documents that we will be looking at and following the timeline from 1991, I want us to come to the point where the joint -- where the staff of the joint forces was set up in 1995 in order to try and show you what the genesis of the formation of the joint forces was and what their tasks were. The action under the name of Poskok is proposed here. Under items 1 through 8, the tasks of the units of the special police in that particular action are detailed. When we turn to page 2 we will be able to see that the document was approved by the assistant minister and deputy minister Mr. Tomljenovic was also in agreement with that proposal. Let us go back to page 1, although I should first ask you, Mr. Theunens, have you ever seen the document and have you taken it into consideration in your analysis?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen this document. I am familiar with operations of special police units in the Velebit Mountains, and if I had had the documents I would have included it, even if it was just for historical purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'm sure you would. [Interpretation] Let's have a look at the task of the units of the special police in the situation such as this one in the course of Operation Poskok in the area of Velebit. utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- it's in the Croatian text, Diverzantsko-Teroristicka Grupa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's it. [Interpretation] Therefore, locating sabotage terrorist groups, their capturing, disarmament, bringing in or destroying. The task specified there is work on locating all types of arms and ammunition hidden, various hideouts and camps in the Velebit area. Item 6, locating undetected human bodies, graves and identification through an on-site investigation. The items between 3 and 6 actually clearly define the tasks and goals of the special police after Operation Storm in the so-called cleanup operations. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I just see 3 again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the bottom of the previous page. Indeed, and I have -- most of the documents I have seen that cover the operations conducted by special police units after Operation Storm address item 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What about item 4, 5, and 6?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 4, I have no specific recollection. I don't claim that it was not the case, but I know that there is, for example, prior to a clearing operation the special police, i.e., General Markac, requests through the chief of the Main Staff updated maps, and I have seen -- and these are included in part 2 of the report, orders -- or at least one order by General Cervenko to General Gotovina, as well as General Markac, to provide maps of the wider Knin area with assessed locations of minefields. utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for your answer. That -- that is like it is.

utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number D1089.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And excuse me, I made an error in -- when I gave the names. This is page 52, line 11. It was General Gotovina as well as General Cermak. I apologise for this error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Yes. D1089 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: May I have 3D01-0678.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Chronologically speaking, we are now in 1993. We'll see a document sent by General Markac, who was the head of the special police sector. It was sent to the heads of police administrations and was also supposed to be delivered to the commanders of the special police units and to the commander of the anti-terrorist group Lucko, which was not a part of the police administration's system, and it was directly under the seat of the ministry and the sector of special police. utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to read the whole document. It's a pity because it's just electronically but just to check the various paragraphs but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes. We will come to each and every paragraph. I'm just asking you about the first one.

utterances.text: Yeah, and I think the introduction is also important because the introduction, in my view, suggests that there have been -- that there are changes or at least proposals for changes in the internal structure of the Ministry of Interior as well as special police field of activities, as it is translated. utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One can then see from the document that the use of joint forces of the special police is defined pursuant to the needs in the field, that is to say that it is an ad hoc special purpose unit that was supposed to carry out tasks as define in item 1 in the territory of one or several police administrations.
